sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 38 & 53/2011-12 dated 04.08.2023 in respect of Sy. No.117 (old 79) measuring 8708 Sq. feet of Shettigere village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.
A.P. No.43/2024 .2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.117 (old 79) measuring 8708 Sq. feet of Shettigere village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka,
Bengaluru Urban District has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010.

Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded compensation for the acquired land @ Rs. 150 lakhs per acre for agricultural land and Rs. 1,314/-
per acre for converted land as compensation for the acquired land.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application on 01.12.2011 for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/38 & 53/2011-12 dated 04.08.2023.
.4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section A.P. No.43/2024 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the respondent No.3 Arbitrator committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents by the petitioner side for deciding the market value and enhancing the market value in the proceedings before him while passing the market value in the proceedings before him while passing the impugned award.

Further stated that while fixing the market value the acquiring authorities have to follow the procedure of taking the sale statistics, it is a settled law that highest sale statistics has to be taken into account in fixing the market value and not the average of sale statistics.

Further submits that the Arbitrator has held that, the compensation paid by the authority for the acquired land at Shettigere village was less as compare to the Arbitral Award already passed with respect of other village.

The Arbitrator failed to consider A.P. No.43/2024 the fact that inspite of land was Ashwin Rajendra vs The Project Director Technical ... on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144119591/
2 converted for non-agricultural land, the respondent No.2 has awarded compensation under non-developed area at the rate of Rs.876/- instead of Rs. 1314/- per Square feet, but the inspite of observation of this Arbitrator has enhanced only Rs. 1749/- per Square feet.

sentences.text: The Arbitral Award dated 04.08.2023 is contrary to the substantive provisions of law.

The Arbitrator has not complained the Section 31 (5 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act) by providing free copy of Arbitral Award to the petitioner and the Arbitral Award is not in accordance with the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The award of the Special Deputy Commissioner - 3 and Arbitrator,
Bengaluru Urban Bengaluru passed an award dated 04.08.2023 but the Arbitrator has not sent copy of the award.
Now only the petitioner filed the application before the Arbitrator for certified copy of Arbitral Award and the same was received.

Among other A.P.
No.43/2024 grounds

, prayed to set aside the award dated 04.08.2023.
.5.

The learned advocate for respondents 1 and 2 on 17.09.2025 filed a memo stating that they have paid enhanced compensation amount to the petitioner with copy of the document for having been paid the enhanced compensation of Rs. 2,89,43,730/- and claimed that the petitioner received the said amount as full and final settlement and without protest.
Accordingly claimed that the dispute reached finality and prayed to dismiss the petition.

.6. The learned Advocate for petitioner filed detailed objection particularly claiming that there is no bar to file appeal after receiving the compensation amount and prayed for dismissal of memo and allow the petition.
.7. The petitioner and respondent 1 and 2 advanced their arguments both on main petition and memo and consented to dispose off the memo along with petition.
The respondent No.3 though served with the notice, not appeared before the Court through their advocate.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-38 & 53/2011-12 dated 04.08.2023 secured from the Arbitrator.

.9. On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that:
1)Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) Whether the respondents 1 and 2 prove that the petition is not maintainable in view of the payment of enhanced compensation?
3) What order?

sentences.text: Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my finding on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 In the negative Point No.2 : In the affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
A.P. No.43/2024 REASONS .11. POINTS 1 and 2: These two points are interlinked with each other hence taken up together for common discussion.
.12.
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner Ashwin Rajendra is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.117 (old 79) measuring 8708 Sq. feet of Shettigere village,
Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Additional Taluka and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 1,314/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that the compensation amount was disbursed to the petitioner.

It is further admitted and proved the fact that the petitioner had received the enhanced compensation of Rs. 2,89,43,730/- and the document produced by the respondent No. 1 and 2 regarding payment of said amount is not disputed by the petitioner.
Hence the said document produced along with memo dated 17.09.2025 can be accepted by the court.
As per the said document, the petitioner received the said amount as full and final settlement without protest and no more claim left on SLAO by the petitioner.

When the petitioner had received the enhanced compensation by stating that no more claim left on SLAO by the petitioner and he had received the amount as full and final settlement and also without protest certainly this petition is liable to be dismissed.
In view of the receipt of enhanced compensation, certainly this petition becomes infructuous as the amount of compensation decided by the Arbitrator reached the finality.
When the dispute reached the finality, certainly this petition is liable to dismissed.
The only contention raised by the petitioner A.P. No.43/2024 to the memo is that there is no bar to file a appeal after receiving of the compensation.
The said contention cannot be accepted particularly when the petitioner stated that no claim left and received the amount as full and final settlement without protest.
As such, the petitioner is estopped from continuing with this petition.
.14. In view of the aforesaid fact of receiving the enhanced compensation, this court left with no option to confirm the award passed by the respondent No. 3.

Hence,
merits of the petition are not discussed.

Accordingly this court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner failed to make sufficient grounds to intervene with the Ashwin Rajendra vs The Project Director Technical ... on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144119591/
4 Judgment and Award passed by the Arbitrator but the memo filed by the respondent 1 and 2 has to be accepted and petition is liable to be dismissed.

.15. Point No.3:

A.P. No.43/2024 ORDER Petition filed under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 R/W Section 3-G(6) of the National Highways Act, 1956 by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.

Consequently, the award passed by the respondent No.3 in case No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-7 / CR / 38 & 53 /2011-12 dated 04.08.2023 in respect of Sy. No.117 (old 79) measuring 8708 Sq. feet of Shettigere village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl.
Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District is hereby confirmed.
